explanation: Dutch Brazil was the American theatre of this war and not an enterprise beside it. The war's article, at revision 1374150566, describes a conflict in which "the Dutch companies and fleet" were "invading Portuguese colonies in the Americas, Africa, and the East Indies"; the Dutch Brazil article dates the American half of that to the fleet of sixty-five ships under Hendrick Corneliszoon Loncq, which "gained control of Olinda by 16 February 1630, and Recife (the capital of Pernambuco) and António Vaz by March 3". `enabled` rather than `caused`: the war is what made a Company fleet in Brazilian waters possible, and the colony is one of the things that possibility was spent on. The atlas also files the colony under the war as a part of it; `parent` does not enter the adjacency, so the causal reading is written here or nowhere.
